content_voiceover: This slide covers the two prognostic scoring systems used for Waldenström macroglobulinemia. The original International Prognostic Scoring System, ISSWM, assigns one point each for age sixty five or older, hemoglobin eleven point five or below, platelets one hundred thousand or below, beta-2 microglobulin above three, and monoclonal IgM above seven grams per deciliter. Patients are then grouped as low risk with a score of zero or one excluding age alone, intermediate risk if age or a score of two, and high risk with a score of three or more. The Revised ISSWM refines this by grading age more finely, zero points under sixty five, one point for sixty six to seventy five, and two points above seventy five, then adds one point each for beta-2 microglobulin above four, LDH above two hundred fifty, and albumin below three point five. This produces five risk groups from very low, score zero, up to very high, score four or five, and the prognostic separation is dramatic, three year WM-specific mortality ranges from zero percent in the very low group up to forty eight percent in the very high group, and ten year overall survival ranges from eighty four percent down to just nine percent. This kind of granular risk stratification is exactly the sort of detail boards like to test.
keypoints: ISSWM: age 65+, Hb ≤11.5, platelets ≤100, beta-2M >3, IgM >7 each worth 1 point
Revised ISSWM grades age (0/1/2 points) and adds LDH >250 and albumin <3.5
Five risk groups: very low to very high, based on total score
10-year OS spans roughly 84 percent (very low) down to 9 percent (very high)
keypoint_voiceover: Know that Revised ISSWM adds LDH and albumin to a graded age score, producing five risk tiers with a striking spread in both three-year mortality and ten-year survival.
